newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai city agriculture output value up 5.8 pct.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai city agriculture output value up 5.8 pct.

text.p: Shanghai's total agriculture output value for 1996 was 19.8 billion yuan, up 5.8 percent on the previous year and accounting for 2.6 percent of China's total, official statistics released on Wednesay showed.

Of Shanghai's total agriculture output, plant production value was 8.49 billion yuan, up 7.3 percent, and animal breeding 8.61 billion yuan, up 6.9 percent, the figures from the city's statistical bureau showed.
The value of production of aquatic products fell 7.8 percent to 2.65 billion yuan.
Spring grain production in Shanghai totalled 4.3 billion kg.

The recently introduced "vegetable basket project" under which townships are encouraged to supply food to nearby cities now guaranteed supplies of agricultural products and prices remained stable, the bureau said.
The numbers showed grain production was 2.12 million tonnes, up 2.8 percent, cotton production was 4,000 tonnes, up 3.7 percent, and oil seeds production was 1.62 million tonnes, up 2.7 percent.
Fruit production was 1.95 million tonnes, down 10.1 percent.
Meat production totalled 2.46 million tonnes, up 2.1 percent on the 1995 figures, with pork accounting for 2.43 million tonnes of the total, up 1.7 percent on 1995.
Milk production totalled 2.18 million tonnes, the same as in 1995, the data showed.
Total 1996 exports of agriculture products produced by Shanghai were valued at 640 million yuan, up 13.9 percent on 1995, with direct exports worth 520 million yuan, up 13.2 percent
